packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect: Effects: serializable descriptions of a single change to Jira or to a structure (`StoredEffect`), the extension point that turns them into executable changes (`EffectProvider`, `Effect`, `EffectResponse`), and ready-made factory methods for common issue changes (`CoreEffects`). Effects are produced by effectors and applied later by the plugin's effector process engine.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectba: Internal bookkeeping for undo and redo of forest actions performed through generators. Types here are marked internal; they are public only so that the plugin's modules can share them, and third parties should not rely on them.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector: Effectors: an extension point for automation that walks a forest and proposes changes (effects) for the items in it. Contains the `Effector` module interface, the function it returns, the collector and context it receives, its response type and its well-known parameter names.

Persistent effector instances: an effector module key plus saved parameters, optionally attached to a structure (they appear as effector rows in that structure). Provides the read model and a manager for creating, reading, updating and deleting them.

Effector processes: the asynchronous, persistent jobs that first compute a preview of effects and then apply them, with per-effect records and undo. Provides the process read model, its status lifecycle, the records and the manager service used to start, confirm, cancel, undo and query processes.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.error: Error reporting for the whole API: the checked `StructureException` with its builder, the `StructureError` code interface with categories, the built-in catalogue of error codes `StructureErrors`, and two auxiliary exception classes.
packages.com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event: Change notifications about Jira issues and links as seen by the plugin (`IssueEventBridge`, `IssueListener`, `JiraChangeEvent` and subclasses, `JiraChangeType`), plus two plain event objects the plugin publishes on the Jira event publisher (`StructureDeletedEvent`, `StructureItemConvertedEvent`).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.C.summary: Static factory methods that build `StoredEffect` values understood by the effect providers bundled with the plugin. It cannot be instantiated. Each method only builds an immutable description; nothing is changed until an effector process applies the effect, at which point the change is made on behalf of the process owner with Jira's normal issue update rules and permissions. Every result names a bundled provider module by its complete key (the plugin key followed by `:` and the module name given per method below) and carries the issue as parameter `issue` (the issue id, a `Long`). A null `issue` (or a null collection or custom field) causes a `NullPointerException`. The notification flag parameter is not set by these helpers. Methods that take a `CustomField` first check its type and throw `IllegalArgumentException` if the field's type is not the expected Jira custom field type (or, for version and group pickers, if its single/multiple setting does not match).

Builds a warning pseudo-effect. It is shown in the process preview but never applied and never produces an effect record; a preview that contains only warnings finishes without applying anything. com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.E.summary: A ready-to-run change, returned inside a valid `EffectResponse` by an `EffectProvider`. Implemented by effect providers (usually as a lambda). The plugin calls it at most once, while applying an effector process, on a background thread with the process owner as the current user.

members.apply(): Performs the change and returns a `StoredEffect` that would undo it (the plugin saves it in the effect record and uses it for undo processes). Must not return null. Throw `StructureException` to report a failure: the plugin records an error record using the exception's localized text and continues with the next effect. Other runtime exceptions are also caught and recorded as a generic apply failure.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effect.E.summary: Extension point that knows how to validate, describe and execute one kind of `StoredEffect`. Other plugins register implementations as effect-provider modules in their plugin descriptor; a stored effect selects its provider by the module's complete key (`StoredEffect.getModuleKey()`). The plugin calls the provider while computing an effector preview (`optimize`, then `resolve` for validation) and again when applying (`resolve`, then `Effect.apply()`).

Checks the stored effect against the current state of Jira and the current user's permissions and returns an `EffectResponse`: valid (with the executable `Effect`, a success message, a description and the affected items), error (with the reason), or empty (nothing to do, e.g. the value is already set). Must not return null and should not change anything itself. It may be called more than once for the same effect (once during preview, once just before applying). During preview an error response turns the effect into a warning and an empty response drops the effect (unless it carries a `conflicts` parameter); during apply an empty response produces no record and an error response produces an error record.

Lets a provider merge or drop redundant effects (for example, several updates of the same field of the same issue). The default returns the input unchanged. The bundled providers keep the last value per issue and field and attach the overridden values to it as a `conflicts` parameter. Must not return null.

members.<init>(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.u: Creates the response from a description and the affected items (both expected non-null, not checked). Same as `EffectResponse.empty`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectba.summary: Internal record of the effects of one user action performed on a generated forest (for example moving rows that makes generators change issues), kept so that the action can be undone and redone. Not intended for third-party use.

members.spec: The forest specification the action was performed on.
members.version: The forest version right after the action; undo/redo re-applies row replacements only if the forest's version signature still matches.
members.movedRows: Ids of the rows the user moved in the action.
members.effects: The generator effects performed, in order, each with its inverse.
members.redoReplace: Rows to substitute in the forest when the batch is redone; null if not applicable.
members.undoReplace: Rows to substitute in the forest when the batch is undone; null if not applicable.

members.timestamp: Time of creation or last undo/redo, from `System.nanoTime()` (only meaningful for comparisons within one JVM). Used to expire batches.
members.userKey: Key of the user who performed the action (the current user at construction; may be null for anonymous).
members.<init>(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.f: Creates a batch from, in order: the forest spec, the forest version, the moved rows, the redo replacement, the undo replacement and the effect pairs. Sets state to `APPLIED`, the timestamp to now and the user key to the current user.

members.effect: The effect as performed (re-run on redo).
members.inverse: The effect that reverses it (run on undo); null if it cannot be undone.
Creates a pair from, in order: generator row id, external flag, effect, inverse (nullable).

The plugin's implementation keeps them in memory only (lost on restart), and expires batches about 71 seconds after they were stored (configurable); loading a batch does not extend this. Expired batches are removed by a cleanup that runs about every 35 seconds, so a batch can stay loadable for up to about 106 seconds. Not intended for third-party use.

Stores the batch and returns a new id for it. Ids are unique within the running node; the high 32 bits identify the node's runtime instance.
members.loadBatch(long): Returns the batch with the given id, or null if it does not exist, has expired, was recorded by another runtime instance, or belongs to a different user than the current one (unless security checks are overridden).

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effectba.summary: Internal: whether an `EffectBatch` is currently in effect or reverted.

Arguments: the instance or one-off parameters (never null, possibly empty) and the context, through which the effector must request any attribute values it needs (requests made after this method returns are ignored). Return `EffectorFunctionResponse.valid` with the function, or an errors response; error texts are turned into warnings in the preview and the effector produces no effects. Called on a background thread with the process owner as the current user; must not return null.

Throw `EffectorUnavailableException` if the effector cannot be configured now; its localized message is shown to the user.
Fills the configuration form for editing an existing instance. Arguments: the saved instance parameters (read-only) and the mutable map of form variables to fill. Throw `EffectorUnavailableException` if the effector cannot be configured now.

Arguments: the submitted form (keys are field names, values usually arrays of strings as delivered by the web layer) and an error collection to which validation errors are added (field errors appear next to the fields; any error makes the plugin show the form again instead of saving). Returns the parameters to save; must not return null and values must be JSON-compatible. The plugin adds `effectorName` itself. Throw `EffectorUnavailableException` if the effector cannot be configured now.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.summary: Context passed to `Effector.getEffectorFunction`. Implemented by the plugin, one per process; not thread-safe.

members.requireAttribute(com.almworks.jira.struc: Declares that the effector function needs the given attribute. The plugin loads all declared attributes for all rows of the forest in one consistent snapshot and passes them as `RowValues` to `EffectorFunction.produceEffects`. Calling it more than once with the same spec has no extra effect.
members.getForestSpec(): The forest the process runs on: for effector instances, the structure that owns the instances; for one-off runs, the forest spec given to `EffectorProcessManager.startProcess`. Never null.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.summary: The working part of an effector, returned by `Effector.getEffectorFunction` inside a valid `EffectorFunctionResponse`. Implemented by effector authors. Called once per process (per instance) on a background thread with the process owner as the current user.

Should stop early when the sink reports cancellation. Must not modify anything itself. An exception thrown here fails the calculation (status `CALCULATION_FAILED`) with the exception's message.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.summary: Result of `Effector.getEffectorFunction`: either `Valid` with a function or `Errors` with at least one message. Immutable; created only through the static factories (the constructor is private, so there are no other subclasses).

members.valid(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.ef: Returns a `Valid` response wrapping the function (expected non-null, not checked).
members.error(String, Object[]): Returns an `Errors` response with one message, built from an i18n key and its arguments.
members.errors(com.almworks.jira.structure.api.u: Returns an `Errors` response with the given messages in order. Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if none are given.
members.errors(java.util.List): Returns an `Errors` response with the given messages in order (the list is kept, not copied). Throws `IllegalArgumentException` if the list is empty.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.summary: Failure variant of `EffectorFunctionResponse`. Each message becomes a warning in the process preview.

members.getEffectorFunction(): The function to run; never null when created properly.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.summary: Checked exception an `Effector` throws from its form methods when it cannot be configured at the moment (for example a required feature or another plugin is missing). Carries a separate message for logs and for users.

members.<init>(String): Creates the exception with one text used both as the log message and as the user-facing localized message.
members.<init>(String, String): Creates the exception with a log message (first argument) and a user-facing, already localized message (second argument).
members.getLocalizedMessage(): The user-facing message given at construction (equal to `getMessage()` when the one-argument constructor was used). The plugin shows it as the error of the configuration dialog.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.summary: A saved effector configuration: effector module key, parameters and the owning structure. Instances are created by the plugin (returned by `EffectorInstanceManager.getEffectorInstance`) and are immutable value objects; equality covers all four properties. In a forest an effector instance appears as an item of the effector item type with the same id.

members.getModuleKey(): Complete module key of the `Effector` this instance runs. Never null.
members.getParameters(): The saved parameters as an unmodifiable map (empty if none were saved). Never null.
members.getOwningStructure(): Id of the structure the instance belongs to, or null if it is not attached to any structure. Only instances with an owning structure can be run.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.summary: Service for persisting effector instances. Implemented by the plugin and obtained as an OSGi component (injection). Data is stored in the plugin's database tables and cached. Changes are recorded as item changes so that forests showing the instances refresh. Note: the implementation performs no permission checks; callers must check that the current user may configure effectors in the owning structure.

members.createEffectorInstance(String, java.util: Creates and saves a new instance and returns its id. Arguments: the effector's complete module key (not checked against installed effectors), the parameters (null or empty stores none; must be serializable to JSON) and the owning structure id (nullable). The plugin's implementation never throws `StructureException` here; it fails with an unchecked exception if the plugin is stopped or storage fails.
members.getEffectorInstance(long): Returns the instance with the given id. If loading fails it throws an unchecked `StructureRuntimeException`, not the declared `StructureException`. Although declared not-null, the plugin's implementation returns null when no instance has that id; callers should handle null.
members.updateEffectorInstance(long, String, jav: Replaces the module key, parameters and owning structure of an existing instance. Arguments in order: instance id, new module key, new parameters (null or empty clears them), new owning structure id (null detaches). Throws `StructureException` with `ITEM_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` if the id does not exist.
members.deleteEffectorInstance(long): Deletes the instance with the given id. Deleting a missing id silently does nothing. Does not remove rows referring to it from forests.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.summary: The persisted result of applying one preview effect in an effector process: success message or error, the undo effect and the affected items. Created by the plugin while applying and read through `EffectorProcessManager.getEffectRecords`. Immutable value object.

members.getProcessId(): Id of the effector process the record belongs to.
members.getEffectMessage(): On success, the provider's success message; on failure, the error message. Never null.
members.isError(): True if the effect could not be applied (no provider, provider returned an error, or applying threw).
members.getUndoEffect(): The effect that reverses this change, as returned by `Effect.apply()`; null for error records.
members.getAffectedItems(): Identities of the items the effect touched, as reported by the provider; never null (empty if unknown, e.g. when no provider was found).
members.getTimestamp(): When the effect was applied, in epoch milliseconds.
members.getPreviewIndex(): Zero-based index of the effect in the process preview list (`EffectorPreview.getPreviewEffects()`); used to resume interrupted processes and to select records for undo.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.summary: The calculated outcome of the calculation phase of an effector process: the list of effects that will be applied, or the errors that stopped the calculation. Immutable as returned by the plugin.

members.getErrors(): Errors that made the calculation fail (status `CALCULATION_FAILED`). Never null; empty when calculation succeeded.
members.getPreviewEffects(): The effects to apply, in application order, after provider optimization and validation; may include warning pseudo-effects, which are shown but not applied. Never null.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.summary: A snapshot of an effector process: a persistent background job that first calculates a preview of effects and then applies them. Returned by `EffectorProcessManager`; immutable, so re-read it to see progress. Progress percentages and cancellation are tracked by a separate process handle.

members.getProcessHandleId(): Id of the plugin's generic process handle that tracks this process's progress and cancellation in the UI.
members.getEffectorPreview(): The preview, if one is stored: set when calculation finishes or fails, and cleared (null) again when the process completes or is stopped. Null while pending or calculating.
members.getUserKey(): Key of the user who started the process; effects are applied on that user's behalf. Never null.
members.getStartTime(): Epoch milliseconds when calculation started, overwritten with the time applying started; null if the process has not started yet.
members.getFinishTime(): Epoch milliseconds when the last phase ended (calculation finished, failed or stopped; applying completed or stopped). Reset to null while applying is in progress; null before the first phase ends.
members.getRevertedProcessId(): For an undo process, the id of the process it reverts; null for normal processes.
members.isAcknowledged(): True once the owner has dismissed the finished process (see `EffectorProcessManager.acknowledgeFinished`). Unacknowledged processes are those listed by `getRunningProcessesForUser`.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.summary: Lifecycle status of an effector process. Normal flow: `PENDING` -> `CALCULATING` -> `CALCULATED` (only when confirmation is required) -> `QUEUED` -> `IN_PROGRESS` -> `COMPLETED` or `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS`. A process whose preview is empty or contains only warnings goes straight to `COMPLETED`.

members.PENDING: Created and waiting for its calculation to start.
members.CALCULATING: The effectors are running and the preview is being computed.
members.CALCULATED: The preview is ready and waits for the user to confirm (`confirm`) or discard (`deleteCalculated`).
members.CALCULATION_FAILED: Calculation failed; the errors are in the preview's `getErrors()`.
members.CALCULATION_STOPPED: Calculation was cancelled by the user, or abandoned because the node restarted while calculating.
members.QUEUED: Waiting in the apply queue; processes are applied one at a time, oldest queued first.
members.COMPLETED: Applying finished with no error records (also used for previews with nothing to apply).
members.COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS: Applying finished but at least one effect produced an error record, or applying aborted with an unexpected error.
members.APPLY_INTERRUPTED: Applying (or waiting in the queue) was cut short by a node shutdown or failover; can be continued with `resumeInterrupted`.
members.APPLY_STOPPED: Applying was cancelled by the user; the effects already applied stay applied.

com.almworks.jira.structure.api.effector.summary: Service to start, observe and control effector processes. Implemented by the plugin and obtained as an OSGi component (injection). All methods act as the current user. Processes are stored in the database and run on background jobs: calculation runs right after start; applying is done by a periodic job (about every 2 seconds) that takes one queued process at a time, cluster-wide on a single node. Methods that take a process id throw `StructureException` with the plugin's own error 6017 `ENTITY_NOT_EXISTS_OR_INACCESSIBLE` (category `NOT_FOUND`; see SPEC.md, the plugin's own error codes) unless the current user started the process, is a Jira administrator, or security checks are overridden.

members.validateStartProcess(java.util.List, lon: Checks, without starting anything, that the current user may run the given effector instances from the given structure. Same checks and exceptions as `startProcess(List, long, boolean)`.
members.validateStartProcess(String, java.util.M: Checks, without starting anything, that the current user may run a one-off effector. Same checks and exceptions as `startProcess(String, Map, ForestSpec, boolean)`; the parameters are not validated.
members.startProcess(java.util.List, long, boole: Starts a process that runs the given saved effector instances and returns its id. Arguments: the instances (not empty), the id of the structure the user runs them from, and whether the preview must be confirmed before applying (if false, a non-empty preview is queued for applying automatically). Instances are evaluated in forest order by depth, then position; each sees the sub-forest under its row's parent. Throws `StructureException` with `EFFECTOR_EXECUTION_DENIED` if the user lacks the global permission to execute effectors, or if an instance belongs to a structure other than the given one and the user lacks the permission to run effectors on queries; with `INVALID_PARAMETER` if the list is empty, an instance's module is not installed or an instance has no owning structure; with `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` if the user cannot view an owning structure. Problems found later (instance row missing or duplicated in the forest) make the process fail with `CALCULATION_FAILED`.
Starts a one-off process that runs an effector with the given parameters over the given forest, without a saved instance, and returns its id. Arguments: the effector's complete module key, its parameters, the forest spec and the confirmation flag (as above). Throws `StructureException` with `EFFECTOR_EXECUTION_DENIED` if the user lacks the global permission to execute effectors or the permission to run effectors on queries; `INVALID_PARAMETER` if no such effector is installed; `STRUCTURE_NOT_EXISTS_OR_NOT_ACCESSIBLE` if the forest spec refers to a structure the user cannot view.
members.startUndoProcess(long, java.util.Collect: Starts a process that reverts the applied effects of a finished process and returns the new process id. Arguments: the process to revert and the preview indexes of the records to revert (null means all successful records). The undo effects of the selected successful records are queued for applying immediately, without confirmation, in record order. Throws `StructureException`: `EFFECTOR_EXECUTION_DENIED` without the global execute permission; not-found if the process is not accessible; `INVALID_PARAMETER` if the process status is not `COMPLETED`, `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS`, `APPLY_INTERRUPTED` or `APPLY_STOPPED`, or if no successful record matches.
members.getProcess(long): Returns the current snapshot of the process. Throws `StructureException` if it does not exist or the current user may not see it.
members.getEffectRecords(long): Returns the records of all effects applied so far by the process (successes and errors). Order: Not determined (database order, in practice usually application order); use `getPreviewIndex()` to sort. Same access check as `getProcess`.
members.confirm(long): Confirms a calculated preview so that it is queued for applying. Throws `StructureException` with `INVALID_PARAMETER` if the status is not `CALCULATED`, the preview is missing or it has no effects; with `GENERIC_ERROR` if the status changed concurrently. If the preview contains only warnings, the process is completed instead and nothing is queued.
members.confirm(long, java.util.Collection): Deprecated. Like `confirm(long)`, but when the second argument is not null only the preview effects at those zero-based indexes are kept (out-of-range indexes are ignored; `INVALID_PARAMETER` if none remain) and the stored preview is replaced by that subset before queuing. Null applies all effects.
members.cancel(long): Requests cancellation of a calculating or applying process. Asynchronous: the job notices the request at its next check and the status becomes `CALCULATION_STOPPED` or `APPLY_STOPPED`. Effects already applied are not reverted. A queued process that was cancelled stops as soon as applying begins (`APPLY_STOPPED`). Not determined: the effect on a process waiting for confirmation (`CALCULATED`). Throws `StructureException` with `GENERIC_ERROR` if the process handle cannot be found.
members.acknowledgeFinished(long): Marks a finished process (status `COMPLETED`, `COMPLETED_WITH_ERRORS`, `APPLY_INTERRUPTED` or `APPLY_STOPPED`) as acknowledged, removing it from `getRunningProcessesForUser`. Throws `StructureException` with `GENERIC_ERROR` if the process is in another status.
members.deleteCalculated(long): Deletes a process whose status is `CALCULATED`, `CALCULATION_STOPPED` or `CALCULATION_FAILED`, together with its process handle (used to discard a preview). Throws `StructureException` with `GENERIC_ERROR` if the process is in another status.
members.resumeInterrupted(long): Puts an `APPLY_INTERRUPTED` process back into the apply queue (status `QUEUED`, acknowledged flag cleared); applying continues with the preview effects that have no record yet. Throws `StructureException` with `GENERIC_ERROR` if the process is in another status.

It carries a `StructureError` code and optionally the structure, view, row and item it refers to, a plain message or an i18n key with arguments, and a cause. com.almworks.jira.structure.api.event.Is.summary: Service that fans out issue and link change notifications to registered `IssueListener`s. Implemented by the plugin and obtained as an OSGi component (injection). The plugin feeds it from the Jira event publisher (issue events, field value changes, issue links, remote links, issue properties) and from its own agile integrations.
